LOS ETERNOS: Beyond Sight is an inclusive educational science fiction comic developed by Draw Space for NASA's Space Apps Challenge 2026, addressing the challenge "Abandoned But Not Forgotten."

The story follows KASI, commander of the HANAQ I, who awakens on the Moon after passing through a temporal anomaly, alongside her loyal robot assistant, YACHAY. To return home, they must seek equipment left behind during NASA's lunar missions. However, mysterious entities known as "The Eternals" emerge from these forgotten objects, resentful toward humanity for being abandoned. Their mysterious power could help KASI and YACHAY return home—but will they?

Combining science fiction with information from official NASA sources, our comic transforms lunar exploration, historical missions, and scientific discoveries into an engaging educational adventure.

To make this experience more inclusive, we developed a web platform offering the original illustrated comic, an accessible text-based adaptation with visual descriptions and character dialogues, and voice narration. Designed following WCAG 2.2 accessibility guidelines, it aims to enable people with blindness or low vision to enjoy the same story.

Our project inspires curiosity about space exploration while celebrating NASA's scientific legacy. Because even when missions end, their contributions remain. They are eternal.

🚀🌙 Project Details

LOS ETERNOS: Beyond Sight — An Inclusive Space Comic

LOS ETERNOS is an educational science fiction comic developed by Draw Space for NASA's Space Apps Challenge 2026, addressing the challenge “Abandoned But Not Forgotten.”

Our project transforms the history of equipment NASA has left behind on the Moon into an engaging adventure that celebrates its scientific contributions and makes space exploration more accessible to young audiences, including people with blindness or low vision.

📖 What Does Our Project Do?

The story follows KASI, commander of the HANAQ I spacecraft, and YACHAY, her loyal robot assistant. After passing through a temporal anomaly, they awaken on the Moon and encounter mysterious beings known as The Eternals, entities born from abandoned lunar equipment.

Among them are Eagle, Surveyor 3, Intrepid, and Falcon, inspired by actual NASA missions. Each character carries memories, emotions, and scientific knowledge from its original mission.

To return home, KASI and YACHAY must uncover their stories, rediscover their contributions to humanity, and confront the threat of being forgotten.

Through five chapters and 32 illustrated story pages, the comic combines adventure, friendship, scientific discovery, and the preservation of humanity's technological legacy.

💡 Innovation Highlights

  • Narrative Innovation: We transform historical lunar equipment into characters with personalities, memories, emotions, and unique abilities inspired by their original scientific missions.
  • Scientific Storytelling: We integrate information from official NASA sources into a fictional adventure, helping readers discover real missions, technologies, and scientific achievements.
  • Inclusive Digital Experience: We developed a web platform that offers three ways to enjoy the same story: the original illustrated comic, an accessible text-based adaptation, and voice narration.
  • Accessibility by Design: The web experience uses WCAG 2.2 as a design reference, incorporating structured chapter navigation, visual descriptions, character dialogues, keyboard navigation, and adjustable voice narration.
  • AI-Assisted Creativity: We combined human storytelling and creative direction with artificial intelligence to generate illustrations, maintain visual consistency, and develop an accessible narrative adaptation.

♿ Beyond Sight: How Our Inclusive Platform Works

Our publicly available web platform provides three complementary reading experiences:

1. Visual Reading

Readers can explore the original illustrated comic and download the complete PDF.

2. Accessible Reading

The story is presented in structured HTML, organized by chapters, pages, and panels. Visual descriptions, character dialogues, and narrative context aim to help people with blindness or low vision understand the same story without relying exclusively on illustrations.

3. Voice Narration

Readers can listen to the narrative through browser-based text-to-speech technology, with playback controls and adjustable reading speed, subject to device and browser compatibility.

These three experiences are designed around a shared principle:

One story. Different senses. One universe.

The accessible adaptation is currently an AI-assisted prototype that continues to undergo editorial review and accessibility validation.

💻 Technology Stack

Tool / Technology

Purpose

Canva

Comic layout, graphic design, and page composition.

ChatGPT

AI-assisted illustration generation, visual consistency, storytelling support, and accessible narrative adaptation.

Codex

Web development, content structuring, and accessibility implementation.

HTML5, CSS, JavaScript

Responsive web platform and accessible reading interface.

JSON

Structured comic content, including chapters, pages, visual descriptions, and dialogues.

Web Speech API

Browser-based voice narration and playback controls.

GitHub

Source code management and distribution of the original comic.

Cloudflare Pages

Public hosting of the web platform.

Official NASA Sources

Scientific research and historical documentation.

WCAG 2.2

Technical reference for accessible web design.

🎨 Creative and Design Considerations

Our team considered several factors throughout the development process:

  • Scientific accuracy: Respecting the historical context and scientific contributions of NASA's lunar missions while clearly distinguishing fiction from reality.
  • Visual consistency: Developing a visual bible to maintain the identity of the characters and a distinctive retro 1990s science fiction anime aesthetic.
  • Educational engagement: Turning scientific information into an emotional adventure rather than presenting it as a conventional textbook.
  • Accessibility and inclusion: Designing alternative ways to experience the story without requiring readers to see the original illustrations.
  • Technology accessibility: Creating a lightweight, publicly available website that does not require registration or specialized hardware.
  • Responsible AI use: Combining AI-generated illustrations and narrative assistance with human creative direction, scientific research, and editorial review.

🎯 Expected Impact

Our project aims to inspire curiosity about space exploration, encourage young people to investigate NASA's scientific achievements, and help new generations appreciate the technological legacy of lunar exploration.

By developing an inclusive reading experience, we also aim to reduce barriers that can prevent people with visual disabilities from enjoying illustrated scientific stories.

In the future, this approach could be extended to other educational comics, scientific narratives, languages, and immersive audio experiences.

LOS ETERNOS reminds us that although these machines have completed their missions, their discoveries, memories, and contributions to humanity deserve to be remembered.

Their missions ended. Their legacy lives on. They are eternal.
